summary: Provision policy-aware Slack onboarding bot with Confluence export + archival TTL rules
request_details:
Request: Build and provision a policy-aware Slack onboarding bot that: 1) programmatically creates team channels using a naming template and data-classification tag, 2) enforces channel membership baseline (owners, security-contact, rotation reviewer), 3) wires a per-channel Confluence template and thread-export automation, and 4) applies an archival TTL based on classification (e.g., low=90d, medium=365d, high=manual).

Why: New regulated pods are spinning up faster than we can manually provision channels and link runbooks. We need an automated, auditable flow so legal/security controls are applied consistently and exported thread records exist for audits.

Requested deliverables: a) Slack bot (app) with an approval flow to create channels from a short form, b) Confluence page creation from template and link back in channel topic, c) thread-export job that runs daily for channels marked "export=true" and writes to the linked Confluence page (redacting emails/PII per data-classification guide), d) a policy module that sets archive_at metadata on the channel and schedules archival or requires manual review for "high" classification.

Access/constraints: Must use existing service account pattern, obey RBAC (no cross-tenant access), sign all Confluence create calls with org bot account, and integrate with the existing channel-archival scheduler (INT-624312) so we don't create parallel cron jobs.
impact: Operational friction: manual provisioning causes errors in runbook links and inconsistent retention. Compliance risk: missing thread exports and incorrect retention for regulated teams. Estimated time savings: ~8 hours/week for platform ops across 5 pods.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - this is a provisioning/automation request, not a bug. Example manual repro: 1) Request channel creation in #support, 2) Ops creates channel without classification tag, 3) No confluence runbook is linked, 4) No export job configured. This produces lack of audit trail.
investigation_notes: Spoke with Platform PM (Ravi Singh) and Security (Anya Ruiz) on 2026-03-11. Existing channel-archival service (INT-624312) supports TTL scheduling and can accept 'archive_at' metadata; recommend piggybacking on that rather than adding a new scheduler. Confluence API quota is limited — export job should batch and backoff. Redaction rules: use the canonical Data Classification Guide page referenced above. Need a short-lived service token for export worker; coordinate with SRE for key rotation (see INT-513210 pattern).
security_considerations: Exports must remove or mask email addresses, user IDs, and tokens. Service account must be scoped to only the destination Confluence space and channel metadata. Audit logs must capture who initiated channel creation and who approved the provisioning request.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A Slack app + approval workflow exists; non-admins can request a channel using a form and a designated approver can authorize creation. 2) Created channel topic contains Confluence page link and classification tag. 3) Daily export job runs for channels with export=true and writes a snapshot to the linked Confluence page; exported content is redacted per guide. 4) Channel archival metadata is set according to classification and is recognized by existing archival scheduler. 5) Documentation (Confluence) and runbook for oncall handed to #platform-ops. 6) Unit/integration tests for export redaction logic and RBAC checks.
workaround_instructions: Until automation is live: Platform ops will follow a manual checklist (create channel name with template, add owners/reviewers, create Confluence page from template and paste link, tag channel topic with classification, file an archival job in INT-624312). This is labor-intensive and error-prone; automation is prioritized.
scheduling_constraints: Prefer implementation window during low-traffic hours (weekend deploy) and coordinate with SRE for service account rotation. Confluence API rate limits suggest exports should run in 02:00-05:00 UTC window for US spaces.
